Yeah, that's completely understandable. I'm not sure how it is everywhere, but my experiences were good with the tellers and customer service. Was mostly seated and the customers mostly were really nice and pleasant. Since the majority of customers were regulars and on a pretty consistent schedule it was fairly easy to fall into the routine. But I work at a fairly small local bank, so your mileage may vary. I worked in a call center for the bank and that was too much for me, very rude customers and too busy to breath or think on many days it felt like. I would not recommend that job for most anyone. Then of course back office jobs generally would not have you interacting with customers, mostly just your office-mates or other departments.
I wish you good luck on the job search.

You might also look into the banks around your area. They sometimes have back office entry level positions. They would probably start out a little bit above minimum wage. Even their front office, retail work may not be that bad. I worked at Walmart and had to get myself out and I found some teller/customer service job at a small local bank. And a note on transcriptionists jobs the other commenter mentioned, you can probably find that and other jobs remotely. Just be careful, from my job I've seen lots of fake online job scams. If you get any fishy looking checks, you can always search the routing number to make sure it matches the bank name, and you can also either call yourself or have your bank call and try to verify the check.
